title: bug: source-export accepts a bare or in-repository git binary
description: scripts/local-runner/source-export.mjs (R09b exportSourceSnapshot, openCommit/openRepository) accepts `git: 'git'` and an absolute git inside repoDir. On Windows, a bare 'git' resolves against the repository cwd (task-d72fe292), so repository code can run during export. admission.mjs (CQ-R12, task-44a9e97b) already refuses both before any spawn (see admitCandidate and row A1); export should apply the same guard. Evidence: export with git:'git' and cwd=repoDir runs.
definitionOfDone: exportSourceSnapshot refuses a non-absolute git, and an absolute git whose realpath is inside repoDir, with a fixed EXPORT_* code before any process spawns
A row in scripts/tests/local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs covers the bare, relative and in-repo git cases

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). Load test-driven-development.

In scripts/tests/local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs, add row E9 after E8: 'E9 a bare, relative or in-repository git is refused before any process spawns, and an omitted git comes only from a fully qualified PATH entry outside the repository'. Grep `test('E9` first.
Reuse repo(), tempDir(), put(), exportAt() and failsWith(). Add `delimiter` and `symlinkSync`/`spawnSync` to the existing imports if needed.

The global forbidden patterns apply to test strings too, so never write an eval call.

Setup:
- { dir, head } = repo(t, { a: 'a' }).
- marker = join(tempDir(t, 'moe-ran-'), 'ran').
- The planted git is named 'git.exe' on win32 and 'git' elsewhere. On win32 it is an EMPTY file, which is never executed. On POSIX it is the mode-0755 script '#!/bin/sh\ntouch <marker>\nexit 1\n'. It must not exec a real git: '.' on PATH would make it call itself.
- Plant it at <dir>/<name>, at <dir>/bin/<name> and at <dir>/tools/<name>.

(a) Explicit refusals, on every OS, each failsWith EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID:
- git 'git', 'git.exe', './git', 'bin/git', '..\\git', '\\git.exe' (root-relative on win32) and 'C:git.exe' (drive-relative);
- the absolute join(dir, 'tools', name);
- an absolute git that does not exist, join(tempDir(t, 'moe-nogit-'), name).
The old code reported EXPORT_GIT_FAILED for the last one, after a spawn.

(b) PATH cases. Save process.env.PATH and register a t.after restore BEFORE mutating it; t.after runs FIFO.
1. PATH = `.${delimiter}${delimiter}${saved}`: a relative entry and an empty entry first.
   - exportAt(dir, head, { git: 'git' }) gives EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID.
   - exportAt(dir, head), with git omitted, RESOLVES: its base entries are ['a'], because the resolver skipped both entries and used the real absolute git.
2. PATH = `${join(dir, 'bin')}${delimiter}${saved}`: exportAt(dir, head) with git omitted gives EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID, because the first git on PATH lies inside the repository.

(c) POSIX only, guarded `if (!win32)`:
- A symlink outside the repository, join(tempDir(t, 'moe-link-'), 'git'), pointing to <dir>/tools/git, passed as git, gives EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID.
- After every case, existsSync(marker) === false.
- Positive control: spawnSync(join(dir, 'git')) creates the marker, so its absence above is not vacuous.

Run the file. E9 must fail against today's code: (a) resolves or reports EXPORT_GIT_FAILED, and (b1) runs ./git. Every other row is unchanged and still passes.
implementationPlan.note: Added row E9 (+ delimiter/spawnSync imports). RED verified: 22 pass, E9 fails 'git' resolved instead of EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID. Shared checkout has many peer-dirty paths; touched only the snapshot test file.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/local-runner/source-export.mjs: apply CQ-R12 admission's git guard to the export, before any spawn.

1. readInput:
   - Drop the `git = 'git'` default.
   - Accept git when it is undefined, or when text(git) holds and fullyQualified(git) holds. Anything else is EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID, as today.
   - fullyQualified(p): on win32, the daemon's FULLY_QUALIFIED rule (packages/moe-daemon/src/util/gitExecutable.ts): /^(?:[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|[\\/]{2}[^\\/])/, a drive-absolute or UNC path. Elsewhere, path.isAbsolute(p).
2. New async helper pathGit(). It returns the first regular file named git.com then git.exe (win32), or git (elsewhere), in a fully qualified PATH entry, in PATH order:
   - Split process.env.PATH ?? '' on path.delimiter.
   - On win32 only, trim each entry and strip one pair of surrounding quotes, as the daemon does.
   - Skip empty, relative, drive-relative and root-relative entries.
   - On POSIX the file must also pass access(X_OK).
   - Return null on a miss, and never fall back to a bare name.
   - It only stats; it never spawns.
3. New exported async helper exportGit(repoDir, git):
   - candidate = git ?? await pathGit(). null is EXPORT_GIT_FAILED: no git, which is what a spawn ENOENT gave before.
   - binary = realpath(candidate). A failure is EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID.
   - root = realpath(repoDir), or null when that fails. openRepository then reports EXPORT_REPOSITORY_UNSUPPORTED as today, which keeps E7's codes.
   - Compare with the module's pathKey, which case-folds on win32 and darwin: below = path.relative(pathKey(root), pathKey(binary)). The binary is outside when root is null, below === '..', below starts with '..' + path.sep, or path.isAbsolute(below).
   - Inside the repository is EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID.
   - Return binary, the realpath with its case NOT folded. Running the resolved file closes a symlink re-pointed between the check and the spawn.
4. exportSourceSnapshot: right after readInput, options.git = await exportGit(options.repoDir, options.git), then openCommit(options). No process is spawned before this guard.
5. Header comment: git is absolute, or omitted and resolved by the rule above, and its realpath lies outside the repository. Windows libuv searches the spawn cwd for a bare name (task-d72fe292), so a bare or in-repository git would run repository code as the controller. This mirrors admission.mjs admitCandidate.

admission.mjs is NOT changed. It keeps its own guard, and openRepository and gitRunner are untouched.

Error handling: every refusal stays a fixed EXPORT_* code with fixed text, re-minted by fixedError. The helpers only stat and realpath, and never echo a path.
implementationPlan.note: Added fullyQualified, pathGit, exported exportGit; readInput drops the 'git' default; exportSourceSnapshot runs exportGit before openCommit. Snapshot suite 23/23 green (E9 red->green). admission.mjs/openRepository/gitRunner untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review and read the diff as an attacker:
- Is there ANY path from exportSourceSnapshot to execFile with a git that is not fully qualified, or whose realpath is inside the repository? Check the default path, an explicit path, a symlink, a case variant on win32 or darwin, a UNC path, and a drive-relative path.
- Can PATH inject the repository? Consider a '.', empty, relative or quoted entry, an entry inside the repository, and node_modules/.bin.
- Is the binary that was checked the binary that runs, or can a symlink be re-pointed in between? Is the case-folded key used only for the comparison?
- Do E7's EXPORT_REPOSITORY_UNSUPPORTED cases and E2's EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID cases keep their codes?
- Do the callers that omit git still work on Linux, macOS and Windows CI? Think of /usr/bin/git, Homebrew and Git for Windows' cmd\git.exe.
- Would I be embarrassed if this shipped?
Fix any finding, then re-run step 3's commands fresh before complete_task.
implementationPlan.note: Adversarial review. Path to execFile: exportSourceSnapshot -> readInput (git undefined or fully qualified) -> exportGit (realpath, absolute, outside repo, case-fold only in the comparison) -> openCommit; the realpath is what runs, so a re-pointed symlink cannot swap the binary. A win32 UNC, \\?\ or case variant resolves to the same realpath as root and is refused inside; drive-/root-relative refused by readInput. PATH: '.', empty, relative, quoted entries skipped/stripped; an in-repo entry holding git is refused (fail closed); never a bare-name fallback. E7 (root unreadable falls through to REPOSITORY_UNSUPPORTED) and E2 codes unchanged. Finding fixed: E9's planted git sat only in the repo, so a relative git or relative PATH entry was refused by the realpath failure rather than the fullyQualified rule; added a planted git in a chdir'd cwd outside the repo. Mutation probes (scratch copy): 6/6 killed (drop in-repo check, keep relative PATH entries, drop fullyQualified, bare-name fallback, realpath-failure passthrough, guard removed); unmutated green. Residual (theoretical, same as admission.mjs): repoDir is realpath'd twice (exportGit, openRepository), so a concurrent re-point of repoDir's own path between them is not closed. Final fresh: snapshot suite 23/23 exit 0; X7 pass; daemon context tests 244/244 earlier on identical source-export bytes; Windows Node 22 pass/1 skip (E6).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: exportSourceSnapshot never spawns a git that is not fully qualified, or whose realpath lies inside repoDir. An explicit bare, relative, root-relative, drive-relative, missing or in-repository git is refused with EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID before any process runs. An omitted git resolves to the first git in a fully qualified PATH entry and is held to the same outside-the-repository rule, so existing callers keep working.
acceptanceCriteria: E9 refuses every case and proves that no planted git ran.
Callers that omit git (the E rows, X7 and the four daemon context tests) still pass.
invariants: No spawn happens before the git guard.
Errors are fixed EXPORT_* text only.
admission.mjs, openRepository and gitRunner are unchanged.
compatibility: An explicit absolute git outside the repository, such as the wrapGit logger, still works.
E2 and E7 keep their codes.
approvedScope: source-export.mjs: readInput, pathGit, the exported exportGit, the exportSourceSnapshot wiring, and the header comment

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Rejected alternatives:
- Making git required with no default. Five callers omit git: the snapshot E rows through exportAt, local-runner.test.mjs X7, and four daemon context tests. They would all break, and the four daemon test files would widen the task into a daemon change.
- A safe absolute default, resolved like the daemon's resolveGitExecutable, which keeps every caller working. Note that the daemon's version returns the bare 'git' on POSIX; here POSIX also resolves to an absolute path, which skips '.' and empty PATH entries that execvp would honor.
- Moving the guard into openRepository, shared with admission. It would change landed CQ-R12 bytes and admission's error codes; admission keeps its own guard.
- Refactoring admission.mjs to use exportGit. Out of scope, and it would pull the A rows into the gate.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
admission.mjs readInput requires git and path.isAbsolute. admitCandidate then realpaths repoDir and git (foldCase on darwin, with path.win32.relative folding on Windows), and refuses a binary that is null or not outside the repository with ADMISSION_INPUT_INVALID.

source-export.mjs:
- pathKey already lowercases on win32 and darwin.
- readInput currently defaults git to 'git'.
- gitRunner calls execFile(git, ..., {cwd: root}); a bare name is looked up through PATH, or the cwd on Windows.
- fixedError re-mints refusals.

The snapshot test file:
- defines win32, fixtureEnv (captured at load, so a later PATH change does not affect the git() helper), and wrapGit (POSIX logging wrapper);
- E2 already refuses git '' / 'g\nit' / 7;
- E7's nonRoots are temp dirs plus a missing path, all expecting EXPORT_REPOSITORY_UNSUPPORTED.
planningNotes.risks:
- A planted POSIX git must NOT exec git, or it recurses through '.' on PATH.
- Restore PATH through t.after, registered before mutating it.
- On win32, the planted files are empty and are never executed: an empty git.exe that a buggy resolver picks fails as GIT_FAILED or INPUT_INVALID, never as a success.
- realpath(repoDir) failing must not turn into EXPORT_INPUT_INVALID, which would break E7.
- Never run the case-folded path, because case-sensitive APFS volumes exist.
- The daemon vitest files need the Linux node_modules snapshot recipe, since the shared checkout's node_modules are Windows builds.
